NOTES ON LEARNING ENGLISH

The reading room.
A little closer to the text.

Short teaching notes inspired by the themes of Century Academy’s public Instagram posts: evidence, summary, structure and interpretation.

Follow our Instagram ↗

01 / LITERATURE

Evidence should
do some thinking.

A quotation is not an explanation. After selecting a detail, ask what its wording suggests and why that matters to the question.

TRY THIS QUESTION

What changes in my interpretation if the writer chooses a different word?

That question takes you from spotting a feature to exploring how a writer creates meaning.

02 / LANGUAGE

A summary is
a selection of ideas.

Start with the focus of the question. Select the relevant information, combine related points and express them economically. A passage can become shorter without becoming a useful summary.

Precision matters more than decorative vocabulary. Keep the meaning accurate while using your own phrasing where the task requires it.

03 / WRITING

Let structure
carry the thought.

Longer sentences are not automatically better sentences. Decide which idea matters, then choose a structure that makes its relationship to the next idea clear.

A paragraph should develop a thought. When a new paragraph begins, the reader should understand why.

04 / LITERATURE

Interpretation needs
a reason.

Another reading of a text is valuable when it grows from the language and details on the page. Consider a different interpretation, then test it against the evidence.

These are original teaching notes for the website, rather than quotations or transcripts of Instagram captions.
